title: Night view of La Silla
caption: Night view of La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This night view shows La Silla Observatory, which ESO calls its first observatory, set on the outskirts of the Chilean Atacama Desert. The photograph was taken during the ESO Ultra HD Expedition by Babak Tafreshi.

La Silla sits 600km north of Santiago, at the edge of Chile's Atacama Desert. Today many of ESO's Member States use the site for targeted projects, focused programmes that make use of the telescopes on the site rather than general observing.

Observatories are generally built far from city lights, where dark skies give telescopes the best chance of catching faint light. La Silla, as ESO's first observatory, has a long history of watching the southern sky, and this picture is a portrait of that site at night.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects more light than the eye can, so the night sky appears brighter and richer in stars than it would to a visitor.
